sections.html:
In Wausau the quickest closings come from buyers who do not rely on a mortgage, since loan approval and appraisal are the steps that stretch a listing. The alternatives are hiring an agent or selling the house yourself. Whichever you choose, the paperwork ends the same way: a condition report in the buyer's hands, an electronic transfer return filed online, and a deed on record with Marathon County.

The city is the seat of Marathon County and lies along the Wisconsin River. The 2025 population estimate is 40,188, up 0.5 percent from the 39,994 counted in 2020. The river divides the city into east and west sides, with numbered streets on the east and numbered avenues on the west, which helps when you describe a location to an out-of-town buyer.

Wausau homes cost well under Milwaukee-area suburban prices. The median value of an owner-occupied Wausau home is $167,900 (2020 to 2024), and 57.6 percent of units are owner-occupied.

sections.h2: What Wisconsin requires of a Wausau seller
sections.html:
Selling a building with up to four dwelling units means you owe the buyer a finished condition report, delivered within 10 days of contract acceptance. The rule is in chapter 709. When no report arrives, the buyer may rescind during the two business days after the deadline and get any deposit back. Anyone acting as an estate representative, trustee or court-appointed fiduciary, and never living in the home, is excused.

Sellers also pay the state 30 cents on each $100 of value, or $3 per $1,000, under s. 77.22, at the time of recording. Both parties sign the return online. Section 77.25 exempts several kinds of transfer, including those by will, descent or survivorship.

sections.h2: How property taxes and assessments work in Wausau
sections.html:
Wausau bills may be paid in one lump by January 31 or in three parts, on January 31, April 30 and July 31. Any special assessment on the bill has to be paid in full by January 31. The city clerk's office takes these payments, and Marathon County does not accept payments for the City of Wausau.

Payment choices: ePayments, ACH, participating banks until July 31, the drop boxes at City Hall on Grant Street or across from the post office on Forest Street, postal mail, or in person at 407 Grant Street from 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. A returned electronic payment carries a $45 fee.

The Assessment Department, at 715-261-6600, values property under chapter 70 of the Wisconsin Statutes at the full value obtainable in a private sale. The city's last revaluation was as of January 1, 2020, and the state checks assessments against sales to see whether the citywide ratio stays between 90 and 110 percent of market value. A mailed notice tells you when your assessment changes, and the Open Book period lets you meet an appraiser before any formal appeal.

Marathon County lists a 5x5 short-term loan of up to $5,000 for taxes that are three years or more past due. It is open to applicants who are 55 or older or disabled, and it carries a $3 monthly service charge. Call the county at 715-261-1150 to ask about eligibility.

When money is owed, find the exact payoff before accepting any offer, so your title company can deduct it from proceeds on closing day.

sections.h2: Which Wausau city rules matter before I list?
sections.html:
Property maintenance and rental rules are the two areas most likely to affect a sale. The Inspections and Zoning division, at 407 Grant Street and 715-261-6780, handles complaints and permits. Its rules cover trash containers, parked vehicles and yard signs, and a buyer's agent walking the property will notice any violation.

  • Trash and recycling carts may go out no sooner than 3:00 p.m. the day before pickup and must be removed by 11:00 a.m. the day after. Between pickups the carts belong in a garage, shed, or behind or beside the house.
  • Vehicles may be parked only on hard-surfaced driveway areas, not on the grass. Inoperative or unlicensed vehicles are not allowed on residential lots.
  • Boats, trailers, campers and similar equipment cannot sit in a required front yard or corner side yard except on a hard-surfaced driveway, and anything over 30 feet must be in an enclosed structure.
  • Zoning allows two yard signs at a time, each no larger than 6 square feet and 4 feet high. Real estate signs cannot be placed on boulevards, public right-of-way or utility poles.

If the house is a rental, the division's rental properties page lists rental registration, rental licensing and inspection, and a rent abatement program. Ask which of those apply to your unit before you transfer it.

sections.h2: Recording the deed in Marathon County
sections.html:
Mail the signed original deed, the transfer return receipt and your payment to 500 Forest Street, Wausau. Recording costs $30 a document, and any transfer fee goes in the same payment. Since January 1, 2026 the office returns recorded documents electronically unless you include a self-addressed, stamped envelope, so write your email address on the submission.

Staff at the counter cannot give legal advice, so most deeds come from a title company or an attorney. Certifying a recorded document adds $1, and a copy is $2 for page one and $1 for every page after.

Ahead of the first showing, stroll the yard and curb with the city's rules in your head. Put the carts away between pickups, move any boat or camper onto the hard-surfaced driveway or into an enclosed building, and clear away any vehicle that does not run or lacks current plates. A buyer's agent spots these things before the kitchen, and each one can become a price talk.

If you want a for-sale sign, keep it on your own property and keep to two signs. Gather permit records, ask the Inspections and Zoning division whether anything is open, and keep a payoff figure ready for any tax balance. A cash buyer will want the same folder, so one round of preparation serves every route, and a seller who answers questions fast keeps the deal moving and the closing date intact.

Write down the timing and the net cash for each route.

  • Agent listing. Draws the biggest pool of bidders when the house shows well and you can wait on a loan.
  • Selling on your own. Keeps more of the price but puts disclosures, signs and the contract on you.
  • Cash offer. Aimed at an estate house, a rental with tenants, long-deferred repairs or a short clock. Request the figure on paper, with the name of whoever pays title and recording.

faqs.q: How much does it cost to record a deed in Wausau?
faqs.a: It is $30 a document at the Marathon County Register of Deeds, with any transfer fee from your return receipt added. A copy runs $2 for the first page, then $1 a page. The office is at 500 Forest Street.

faqs.q: When are Wausau property taxes due?
faqs.a: One payment by January 31, or three installments on January 31, April 30 and July 31. Special assessments are due in full January 31. Pay the city, because Marathon County does not collect for Wausau.

faqs.q: Do I have to give a buyer a condition report in Wausau?
faqs.a: For homes of one to four units, yes. Chapter 709 sets a 10-day deadline from acceptance. If the buyer gets nothing, a two-business-day right to rescind follows, though an exempt fiduciary who never lived in the home does not owe the report.

faqs.q: Can I put a for-sale sign in my Wausau yard?
faqs.a: Yes, on your own property. Zoning allows two yard signs at one time, each up to 6 square feet and 4 feet tall. Signs cannot be placed on boulevards, other public right-of-way or utility poles.

faqs.q: What is the Wisconsin transfer fee on a Wausau sale?
faqs.a: The grantor pays 30 cents on each $100 of value ($3 per $1,000) when the deed is filed. A transfer by will, descent or survivorship is exempt under s. 77.25.
